newsitem.title: THAILAND: Exiles urge ASEAN Moslems to avert strife in Burma.
newsitem.headline: Exiles urge ASEAN Moslems to avert strife in Burma.

text.p: Moslem countries in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) should help stop Rangoon from oppressing the Moslem minority in Burma, an exile group said on Tuesday.
The Moslem Liberation Organisation of Burma (MLOB) urged Moslem nations of the seven-member ASEAN to do what they could to help after recent clashes between Buddhists and Moslems in Burma.
For the past 10 days, religious strife has spread through Burma after Buddhist monks went on a rampage in Mandalay and vandalised several Moslem buildings.

The government has said the trouble was started by rumours that a Buddhist girl was molested by a Moslem. Other sources said it was sparked by reports that an important Buddha image in Mandalay had been vandalised.
The problems spread across the country, and witnesses said about 100 Buddhist monks had been detained over the weekend.

Rangoon's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) hopes Burma will be admitted as a full member of ASEAN later this year. ASEAN currently groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Brunei, Indonesia and Malaysia have majority Moslem populations.

"Your continuous efforts to make SLORC a member of ASEAN means that you will assist in making legal the status of SLORC so that they can continue to enslave the people for a longer period of time," said the MLOB letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
ASEAN foreign ministers are expected to discuss admission of new members next month.
"We...would like to urge the three member Moslem countries of the ASEAN grouping to prevent the minority Moslems of Burma from becoming victimised further," the letter said.
